title: Keeping the Body Level: A Moment Wanted, Vertical Forces on the Feet That Give It, and the Largest Push That Can Be Answered

questions.question: Why can the forces on four feet be chosen?
options: Four feet are more than the three conditions (weight, roll moment, pitch moment) need
Each leg has three joints, which is more than a force needs
The weight can be put on any one foot
The floor's friction takes up whatever is left over
questions.explanation: Three equations, four unknown vertical forces. The least norm solution is the one with the smallest sum of squares, and with three feet down there is no choice left.

questions.question: What did each foot carry with no moment wanted?
questions.explanation: The weight of 12 kg is 117.7 N, and with nothing else asked the least norm solution shares it equally among the four feet.

questions.question: What is the largest roll moment that can be given?
options: 10 N m, the largest that was tried
25 N m, limited by the motors
17.7 N m, the weight times the half width
117.7 N m, the weight times one metre
questions.explanation: At 17.7 N m the feet on one side carry everything and those on the other nothing. Any more would need a foot to pull on the floor.

questions.question: A push of 25 N m, with the feet's limit of 17.7 N m:
options: Was answered, with a larger peak roll
Was answered in part, and the body settled at an angle
Rolled the body over (1)
Was scaled down, so the body stayed level
questions.explanation: The feet can supply 17.7 N m and the push was 25. The difference turns the body whatever the gains are.

questions.question: What happens to a moment beyond the limit?
options: It is scaled down, keeping its direction, to the most that can be given
The negative forces are set to zero and the rest are kept
The request is refused and the forces are left as they were
It is given in full by putting more weight on the outer feet
questions.explanation: Setting negative forces to zero leaves forces that add to more than the weight. Scaling the whole moment keeps the sum right and the direction as asked.

questions.question: Why does a trot need a different controller?
options: Its feet are down for too short a time to use
The moments needed in a trot are larger
The least norm solution is too slow at a trot's pace
Two feet cannot give the three conditions
questions.explanation: Two feet on a diagonal give two forces, and three conditions cannot be met with two unknowns. The trot is balanced by where the next feet land.
